Corollary 4.38 implies in particular that the lower semicontinuous envelope of a proper convex function coincides with the function except at most on the relative boundary of its efective domain. Indeed, we have the following result. 

Theorem 4.40. Let $f : \mathbb { R } ^ { m }  ( - \infty , \infty ]$ be a proper convex function. Then lsc f agrees with f everywhere except possibly on $\mathrm { r b } _ { \mathrm { a f f } } \left( \mathrm { d o m } _ { e } f \right)$ . Moreover, for any fixed $z _ { 0 } \in \Gamma \mathrm { i } _ { \mathrm { a f f } } \left( \operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f \right)$ and for any $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ 

$$
f (z) \geq \operatorname{lsc} f (z) = \lim _ {\theta \rightarrow 1 ^ {-}} f ((1 - \theta) z _ {0} + \theta z).\tag{4.19}
$$

Proof. Step 1: Fix any 

$$
z \notin \mathrm{rb} _ {\mathrm{aff}} \left(\mathrm{dom} _ {e} f\right) = \overline {{\mathrm{dom} _ {e} f}} \setminus \mathrm{ri} _ {\mathrm{aff}} \left(\mathrm{dom} _ {e} f\right).
$$

By Proposition 3.12, for every $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ 

$$
\operatorname{lsc} f \left(z\right) = \inf _ {\left\{z _ {n} \right\}} \left\{\liminf _ {n \to \infty} f \left(z _ {n}\right): \left\{z _ {n} \right\} \subset \mathbb {R} ^ {m}, z _ {n} \to z \right\},
$$

and so we may find $\{ z _ { n } \} \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ such that $z _ { n }  z \ \mathrm { a n d }$ 

$$
\operatorname{lsc} f (z) = \lim _ {n \to \infty} f (z _ {n}).
$$

We now distinguish two cases. 

If $z \in \operatorname { r i _ { a f f } } \left( \operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f \right)$ , then since 

$$
\infty > f (z) \geq \operatorname{lsc} f (z) = \lim _ {n \rightarrow \infty} f (z _ {n}),
$$

it follows that $z _ { n } \in \mathop { \Gamma ^ { \mathrm { i } } \mathrm { a f f } } _ { \mathrm { a f f } } \left( \mathop { \mathrm { d o m } _ { e } f } \right)$ for all n suficiently large, and thus, using the continuity of $f$ in $\operatorname { r i } _ { \mathrm { a f f } } \left( \operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f \right)$ (see Corollary 4.38), we obtain that 

$$
\operatorname{lsc} f (z) = \lim _ {n \to \infty} f (z _ {n}) = f (z).
$$

$\operatorname { I f } \ z \not \in { \overline { { \operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f } } }$ , then $z _ { n } \not \in \mathrm { d o m } _ { e } f$ for all n suficiently large, and so 

$$
f (z) \geq \operatorname{lsc} f (z) = \lim _ {n \to \infty} f (z _ {n}) = \infty ,
$$

which concludes the first part of the theorem. 

Step 2: To prove (4.19) fix any $z _ { 0 } \in \Gamma \mathrm { i } _ { \mathrm { a f f } } \left( \operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f \right)$ (note that since $f$ is proper, by Proposition 4.7 we may always find at least one). We again distinguish two cases. 

If $z \in \overline { { \operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f } }$ , then in view of the convexity of $\operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f .$ , by Proposition 4.7 we have 

$$
\theta z + (1 - \theta) z _ {0} \in \mathrm{ri} _ {\mathrm{aff}} (\mathrm{dom} _ {e} f)
$$

for all $0 \leq \theta < 1$ . Hence by Step 1, 

$$
f (\theta z + (1 - \theta) z _ {0}) = \operatorname{lsc} f (\theta z + (1 - \theta) z _ {0})
$$

for all $0 \leq \theta < 1$ . The lower semicontinuous function 

$$
g (\theta) := \operatorname{lsc} f (\theta z + (1 - \theta) z _ {0}), \quad \theta \in [ 0, 1 ],
$$

is convex and real-valued (except possibly at $\theta = 1 )$ , and so continuous in [0, 1]. Therefore 

$$
\begin{array}{l} f (z) \geq \operatorname{lsc} f (z) = g (1) = \lim _ {\theta \to 1 ^ {-}} g (\theta) \\ \quad = \lim _ {\theta \to 1 ^ {-}} \operatorname{lsc} f (\theta z + (1 - \theta) z _ {0}) = \lim _ {\theta \to 1 ^ {-}} f (\theta z + (1 - \theta) z _ {0}). \end{array}
$$

Finally, i $z \not \in \overline { { \mathrm { d o m } _ { e } f } }$ , then $\theta z + \left( 1 - \theta \right) z _ { 0 } \not \in \mathrm { d o m } _ { e } f$ for all $\theta$ suficiently close to one, and so again by Step 1, 

$$
\infty = f (\theta z + (1 - \theta) z _ {0}) = \operatorname{lsc} f (\theta z + (1 - \theta) z _ {0})
$$

for all θ suficiently close to one, which yields (4.19). 

Corollary 4.41. Let $f : \mathbb { R } ^ { m }  ( - \infty , \infty ]$ be a proper convex function and let $C \subset \operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f$ be such that $\overline { { C } }$ is convex. Then 

$$
\inf _ {C} f = \inf _ {\overline {{C}}} f.
$$

Proof. It is enough to show that if $t \in \mathbb R$ is such that $f \left( z _ { 1 } \right) < t$ for some $z _ { 1 } \in \overline { { C } }$ , then $f \left( z _ { 2 } \right) < t$ for some $z _ { 2 } \in C$ . Define 

$$
g \left(z\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} f \left(z\right) \text {if} z \in \overline {{C}}, \\ \infty \quad \text {otherwise}. \end{array} \right.
$$

Since 

$$
\mathrm{ri} _ {\mathrm{aff}} (C) \subset C \subset \mathrm{dom} _ {e} g \subset \overline {{C}},
$$

it follows from Proposition 4.9 that 

$$
\mathrm{ri} _ {\mathrm{aff}} (\mathrm{dom} _ {e} g) = \mathrm{ri} _ {\mathrm{aff}} (C).
$$

Fix any $z _ { 0 } \in \operatorname { r i _ { a f f } } \left( C \right)$ . By (4.19), 

$$
t > f (z _ {1}) = g (z _ {1}) \geq \lim _ {\theta \to 1 ^ {-}} g ((1 - \theta) z _ {0} + \theta z _ {1}),
$$

and thus the result follows by Proposition 4.7. 

Next we extend some of the previous continuity results to the infinitedimensional setting. 

Proposition 4.42. Let $V _ { 1 } , \ldots , V _ { m }$ be locally convex topological vector spaces and let $f : V _ { 1 } \times \ldots \times V _ { m } \to [ - \infty , \infty ]$ be separately convex. $_ { I f f }$ is bounded from above in a neighborhood of a point $v _ { 0 }$ such that $f \left( v _ { 0 } \right) \in \mathbb { R } _ { \mathrm { \Sigma } }$ , then f is continuous at $v _ { 0 }$ 

Proof. Without loss of generality we may assume that $v _ { 0 } = 0$ and that $f \left( 0 \right) =$ 0. For every $i = 1 , \ldots , m$ , let $U _ { i }$ be an open convex neighborhood of the origin in $V _ { i }$ such that 

$$
f (v) \leq a \quad \text { for   all } v \in U _ {1} \times \dots \times U _ {m}
$$

for some $a \in \mathbb { R }$ . We symmetrize the neighborhoods as $W _ { i } : = U _ { i } \cap ( - U _ { i } )$ $i = 1 , \ldots , m$ . Given $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ , we prove that 

$$
| f (v) | \leq m \varepsilon a \quad \text { for   all } v \in \varepsilon \left(W _ {1} \times \dots \times W _ {m}\right).\tag{4.20}
$$

The argument is similar to the one used in Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 4.36. Fix $v \in \varepsilon \left( W _ { 1 } \times \ldots \times W _ { m } \right)$ and write 

$$
v = \left(v _ {1}, \dots , v _ {m}\right),
$$

where $v _ { i } \in V _ { i } , i = 1 , . . . , m$ . By the separate convexity of f we have 

$$
f (0, \dots , 0, v _ {m}) \leq (1 - \varepsilon) f (0) + \varepsilon f (0, \dots , 0, \frac {v _ {m}}{\varepsilon}) \leq \varepsilon a,
$$

where we have used the fact that $( 0 , \ldots , 0 , \frac { v _ { m } } { \varepsilon } ) \in U _ { 1 } \times \ldots \times U _ { m }$ . Again by separate convexity we obtain 

$$
f (0, \ldots , 0, v _ {m}) \geq (1 + \varepsilon) f (0) - \varepsilon f (0, \ldots , 0, - \frac {v _ {m}}{\varepsilon}) \geq - \varepsilon a,
$$

and thus 

$$
\left| f \left(0, \dots , 0, v _ {m}\right) \right| \leq \varepsilon a.\tag{4.21}
$$

Similarly, 

$$
\begin{array}{l} f (0, \ldots , 0, v _ {m - 1}, v _ {m}) \\ \leq (1 - \varepsilon) f (0, \ldots , 0, v _ {m}) + \varepsilon f \left(0, \ldots , 0, \frac {v _ {m - 1}}{\varepsilon}, v _ {m}\right) \\ \leq 2 \varepsilon a \end{array}
$$

by (4.21) and the fact that $\begin{array} { r } { \left( 0 , \dots , 0 , \frac { v _ { m - 1 } } { \varepsilon } , v _ { m } \right) \in U _ { 1 } \times \dots \times U _ { m } } \end{array}$ . Here we have used the convexity of $U _ { m }$ to deduce that $v _ { m } \in \varepsilon U _ { m } \subset U _ { m }$ . Recursively we obtain (4.20). 

More can be said about regularity when f is convex. 

Theorem 4.43. Let V be a locally convex topological vector space and let $f : V  [ - \infty , \infty ]$ be convex. Then the following are equivalent: 

(i) $f$ is a proper function and is continuous in the interior of $\operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f$ , which is nonempty; 

(ii) there exists a nonempty open set on which f is not identically $- \infty$ and is bounded from above. 

Proof. It sufices to show that (ii) implies (i). Let $U \subset V$ be an open set such that 

$$
f (v) \leq a
$$

for all $v \in U$ for some positive constant $^ { a , }$ and fix any $v _ { 0 } \in U$ such that $f \left( v _ { 0 } \right) \in \mathbb { R }$ . By the previous proposition $f$ is continuous at $v _ { 0 }$ , and so in particular, it is finite in a neighborhood of $v _ { 0 }$ . By Remark 4.23 the function $f$ is proper. Let now $v _ { 1 }$ be any point in the interior of $\operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f$ and find a neighborhood $U _ { 1 }$ of $v _ { 1 }$ such that $\begin{array} { r } { U _ { 1 } \subset \mathsf { d o m } _ { e } f } \end{array}$ . By the continuity of the function 

$$
t \in \mathbb {R} \mapsto v _ {0} + t \left(v _ {1} - v _ {0}\right)
$$

at $t = 1$ we may find $t > 1$ such that the point $v _ { t } : = v _ { 0 } + t \left( v _ { 1 } - v _ { 0 } \right)$ is in $U _ { 1 }$ . The continuous invertible function $L : V \to V$ , defined by 

$$
L (v) := \frac {1}{t} v _ {t} + \left(1 - \frac {1}{t}\right) v, \quad v \in V,
$$

maps U into an open set $L \left( U \right)$ and $L \left( v _ { 0 } \right) = v _ { 1 } \in L \left( U \right)$ . Moreover, by the convexity of $f ,$ for any $w \in L \left( U \right)$ , letting $v : = L ^ { - 1 } \left( w \right) \in U$ , we have 

$$
\begin{array}{l} f (w) = f \left(\frac {1}{t} v _ {t} + \left(1 - \frac {1}{t}\right) v\right) \\ \qquad \leq \frac {1}{t} f (v _ {t}) + \left(1 - \frac {1}{t}\right) f (v) \leq \frac {1}{t} f (v _ {t}) + \left(1 - \frac {1}{t}\right) a, \end{array}
$$

which shows that $f$ is bounded from above in a neighborhood of $v _ { 1 }$ . Using again the previous proposition, we conclude that f is continuous at $v _ { 1 }$ , and, given the arbitrariness of $v _ { 1 }$ in the interior of $\operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f$ , this concludes the proof. 

Exercise 4.44. We construct an example of a convex function that is not continuous. Let V be an infinite-dimensional normed space and let $\{ e _ { n } \} \subset V$ be a sequence of linearly independent vectors of norm one. Let $f : V \to \mathbb { R }$ be the linear function satisfying $f \left( e _ { n } \right) : = n$ for all $n \in \mathbb { N }$ and $f : \equiv 0$ outside the span of $\{ e _ { n } \}$ . Prove that $f$ is linear but not continuous. 

If in the previous theorem we assume in addition that f is lower semicontinuous and that V is a Banach space, then we may remove the assumption that $f$ is bounded from above on an open set. 

Corollary 4.45. Let V be a Banach space and let $f : V  ( - \infty , \infty ]$ be a lower semicontinuous convex function. Then f is continuous over the interior $o f \operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f$ 

Proof. Let $v _ { 0 }$ be in the interior of $\operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f$ . By replacing f with $f \left( \cdot - v _ { 0 } \right)$ we may assume, without loss of generality, that $v _ { 0 } = 0$ , so that we may find $B \left( 0 , r \right) \subset \mathrm { d o m } _ { e } f$ . Since $f$ is lower semicontinuous and convex, the set 

$$
C := \{v \in V: f (v) \leq f (0) + 1 \}
$$

is closed and convex and $0 \in C$ . We claim that 

$$
V = \bigcup_ {n = 1} ^ {\infty} n C.
$$

Indeed, if $v \in V , v \neq 0$ , then the function 

$$
g (t) := f (t v), \quad t \in \mathbb {R},
$$

is convex and $\left( - \frac { r } { | v | } , \frac { r } { | v | } \right) \subset \mathrm { d o m } _ { e } g$ . In particular, g is continuous in $\left( - { \frac { r } { | v | } } , { \frac { r } { | v | } } \right)$ , and so there exists $\begin{array} { r } { 0 < \delta < \frac { r } { | v | } } \end{array}$ such that 

$$
| f (t v) - f (0) | = | g (t) - g (0) | \leq 1
$$

for all $| t | \leq \delta$ . Hence tv $\in C$ for all $| t | \leq \delta$ , which implies that $v \in n C$ for all $\begin{array} { r } { n \geq \frac { 1 } { \delta } } \end{array}$ . This proves the claim. 

By the Baire category theorem there exists $n _ { 0 } \in \mathbb { N }$ such that the set $n _ { 0 } C$ has nonempty interior. In turn, C has nonempty interior and thus we may apply the previous theorem to conclude that $f$ is continuous over the interior of $\operatorname { d o m } _ { e } f$ 

Exercise 4.46. Let $V : = L ^ { 1 } \left( [ 0 , 1 ] \right)$ , where the underlying measure is the Lebesgue measure. Show that the functional

defined by

$$
