$$
\begin{array}{l} \int_ {B} f (x, v (x)) d x \geq \int_ {B} h (x, g (x)) d x \geq - \int_ {B} (C (g (x)) ^ {p} + \gamma (x)) d x \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qend{array}
$$

Since this inequality holds for all $v \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ and for every Borel set B, we may apply Proposition 6.24 to deduce 

$$
f (x, z) \geq - C \left(2 ^ {p - 1} | z | ^ {p} + 2 ^ {p - 1}\right) - \gamma (x)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ and for all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ 

The remainder of the proof is devoted to proving claim (6.52). 

Step 3: Let $g \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; [ 1 , \infty ) \right)$ and let $t ~ \in ~ \mathbb { R }$ be any number such that $\begin{array} { r } { t > \int _ { E } J \left( g \right) \left( x \right) } \end{array}$ dx. We claim that there exists $v \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
\int_ {E} f (x, v (x)) d x \leq t, \| v \| _ {L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} \leq 2 \| g \| _ {L ^ {p} (E)}.
$$

Since $\begin{array} { r } { t { \bf \Omega } > \int _ { E } J \left( g \right) \left( x \right) } \end{array}$ dx, by Proposition 1.92 we may find a nonpositive simple function $w \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ such that $\begin{array} { r } { t > \int _ { E } w \left( x \right) } \end{array}$ dx and $w \geq J \left( g \right) \mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. in E with strict inequality whenever $J \left( g \right) \bar { < } 0$ 

By Theorem 1.108 there exists a sequence $\{ v _ { n } \} \subset L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
J (g) (x) = \inf _ {n \in \mathbb {N}} g _ {v _ {n}} (x)\tag{6.55}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. in $E .$ . Let $\tilde { E }$ be the set of points of density one of E at which (6.55) holds. Let $E _ { 0 }$ be the set of all points $x \in { \tilde { E } }$ such that w $( x ) < 0$ , x is a Lebesgue point of $w ,$ a p-Lebesgue point for $g$ and all $v _ { n } ,$ , and a point of approximate continuity for all $g _ { v _ { n } }$ , where all the functions in question have been extended by zero outside $E$ 

Let λ be the measure defined for $B \in B \left( E \right)$ by 

$$
\lambda (B) := \int_ {B} w (x) d x.\tag{6.56}
$$

Then $\lambda ( E \setminus E _ { 0 } ) = 0$ 

If $x \in E _ { 0 }$ , then $J \left( g \right) \left( x \right) \le w \left( x \right) < 0$ , and so $J \left( g \right) \left( x \right) < w \left( x \right)$ . In particular, there exists $n _ { x } \in  { \mathbb { N } }$ such that 

$$
0 > w (x) \geq g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (x),\tag{6.57}
$$

and since $g _ { v _ { n _ { x } } } \left( x \right) < 0$ , it follows from (6.50) that 

$$
g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (x) = f (x, v _ {n _ {x}} (x)),
$$

and in turn, we deduce that 

$$
g \left(x\right) \geq \left| v _ {n _ {x}} \left(x\right) \right|.\tag{6.58}
$$

Fix $\varepsilon > 0$ so small that 

$$
(1 - \varepsilon) \lambda (E) <   t,\tag{6.59}
$$

and find $r _ { x } > 0$ such that for all $0 < r < r _ { x }$ we have 

$$
\left\| v _ {n _ {x}} \right\| _ {L ^ {p} (B (x, r) \cap E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} <   2 \left\| g \right\| _ {L ^ {p} (B (x, r) \cap E)},\tag{6.60}
$$

$$
\frac {\left| \left\{y \in B (x , r) \cap E : \left| g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (y) - g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (x) \right| \geq \varepsilon \right\} \right|}{\left| B (x , r) \cap E \right|} \leq \varepsilon ,\tag{6.61}
$$

$$
\int_ {B (x, r) \cap E} w (y) d y \geq | B (x, r) \cap E | (w (x) - \varepsilon).\tag{6.62}
$$

Note that to obtain (6.60) we have used the fact that x is a p-Lebesgue point for g and $v _ { n _ { x } }$ , (6.58), and the fact that $g \left( x \right) \geq 1$ (this is the first and only time that we use the fact that $g$ is bounded away from zero). 

We observe that for all $0 < r < r _ { x }$ , 

$$
\int_ {B (x, r) \cap E} g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (y) d y \leq (1 - \varepsilon) | B (x, r) \cap E | (g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (x) + \varepsilon).\tag{6.63}
$$

Indeed, since $g _ { v _ { n _ { x } } } \leq 0 \ \mathrm { i f } \ g _ { v _ { n _ { x } } } \ ( x ) + \varepsilon \geq 0$ then the inequality holds. If $g _ { v _ { n _ { x } } } \left( x \right) +$ $\varepsilon < 0$ , then 

$$
\begin{array}{r l} & {\int_ {B (x, r) \cap E} g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (y) d y \leq \int_ {B (x, r) \cap E \cap \left\{\left| g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (\cdot) - g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (x) \right| \leq \varepsilon \right\}} g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (y) d y} \\ & {\quad \leq \left(g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (x) + \varepsilon\right) \left| \left\{y \in B (x, r) \cap E: \left| g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (y) - g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (x) \right| \leq \varepsilon \right\} \right|} \\ & {\quad \leq \left(g _ {v _ {n _ {x}}} (x) + \varepsilon\right) (1 - \varepsilon) | B (x, r) \cap E |,} \end{array}
$$

where we have used (6.61). 

Set $\mathcal { G } : = \{ B \left( x , r \right) : x \in E _ { 0 } , 0 < r < r _ { x } \}$ . By the Vitali–Besicovitch covering theorem there exist disjoint balls $B \left( x _ { 1 } , r _ { 1 } \right) , \ldots , B \left( x _ { k } , r _ { k } \right)$ such that 

$$
\lambda \left(E _ {0} \setminus \bigcup_ {i = 1} ^ {k} B \left(x _ {i}, r _ {i}\right)\right) \geq - \varepsilon .\tag{6.64}
$$

Define 

$$
v \left(x\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} v _ {n _ {x _ {i}}} \left(x\right) \text {   if   } x \in B \left(x _ {i}, r _ {i}\right) \cap E, i = 1, \ldots , k, \\ 0 \qquad \qquad \qquad \text {   otherwise.   } \end{array} \right.
$$

By (6.60) we have 

$$
\| v \| _ {L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} ^ {p} \leq \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} \left\| v _ {n _ {x _ {i}}} \right\| _ {L ^ {p} (B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} ^ {p} \leq 2 ^ {p} \| g \| _ {L ^ {p} (E)} ^ {p}.
$$

Moreover, by (6.50), (6.56), (6.57), (6.58), (6.62), (6.63), and (6.64), since $\lambda \left( E \right) = \lambda \left( E _ { 0 } \right) < t$ and $f \leq 0$ , we have 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \int_ {E} f (x, v) d x \leq \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} \int_ {B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E} f (x, v _ {n _ {x _ {i}}} (x)) d x \\ \qquad \leq \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} \int_ {B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E} g _ {v _ {n _ {x _ {i}}}} (y) d y \\ \qquad \leq (1 - \varepsilon) \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} | B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E | (g _ {v _ {n _ {x _ {i}}}} (x _ {i}) + \varepsilon) \\ \qquad \leq (1 - \varepsilon) \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} | B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E | (w (x _ {i}) + \varepsilon) \\ \qquad \leq (1 - \varepsilon) \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} \int_ {B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E} (w (y) + 2 \varepsilon) d y \\ \qquad \leq (1 - \varepsilon) \lambda (\bigcup_ {i = 1} ^ {k} B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E) + 2 \varepsilon | E | \\ \qquad \leq (1 - \varepsilon) \lambda (E) + \varepsilon + 2 \varepsilon | E | \leq t, \end{array}
$$

provided ε is suficiently small and where we have used (6.59). 

Step 4: Let $g \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; [ 1 , \infty ) \right)$ . We claim that 

$$
\int_ {E} J (g) (x) d x > - \infty .
$$

Indeed, assume by contradiction that $\textstyle \int _ { E } J \left( g \right) ( x )$ dx $= - \infty$ . By Corollary 1.90 we may find a sequence of disjoint sets $E _ { n }$ such that 

$$
\int_ {E _ {n}} J (g) (x) d x = - \infty .
$$

Applying Step 3 to each $E _ { n }$ we may find functions $v _ { n } \in L ^ { p } \left( E _ { n } ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
\int_ {E _ {n}} f (x, v _ {n}) d x \leq - 1, \| v _ {n} \| _ {L ^ {p} (E _ {n}; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} \leq 2 C \| g \| _ {L ^ {p} (E _ {n})}.
$$

Defining 

$$
v := \sum_ {n = 1} ^ {\infty} v _ {n} \chi_ {E _ {n}},
$$

then $v \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ and 

$$
- \infty <   \int_ {E} f (x, v) d x \leq \sum_ {n = 1} ^ {\infty} \int_ {E _ {n}} f (x, v _ {n}) d x \leq \sum_ {n = 1} ^ {\infty} - 1 = - \infty ,
$$

which is a contradiction. 

Step 5: We claim that there exists an integer $k \in \mathbb N$ such that the function $\psi _ { k } : E \to \mathbb { N } \cup \{ \infty \}$ defined by 

$$
\psi_ {k} (x) := \sup \left\{n \in \mathbb {N}: h (x, n) \leq - k n ^ {p} \right\}, \quad x \in E,\tag{6.65}
$$

belongs to $L ^ { p } \left( E \right)$ . Indeed, assume by contradiction that $\textstyle \int _ { E } \left( \psi _ { k } \right) ^ { p } d x = \infty$ for all $k \in \mathbb N$ . By Corollary 1.90 there exist pairwise disjoint Borel sets $B _ { k } \in B \left( E \right)$ such that 

$$
\int_ {B _ {k}} \left(\psi_ {k}\right) ^ {p} d x = \infty \text { for   all } k \in \mathbb {N}.\tag{6.66}
$$

By the definition of $\psi _ { k }$ we may find measurable functions $w _ { k } : B _ { k } \to$ N such that 

$$
h \left(x, w _ {k} (x)\right) \leq - k \left(w _ {k} (x)\right) ^ {p} \text {   for   all   } x \in B _ {k} \text {   and   } \int_ {B _ {k}} \left(w _ {k}\right) ^ {p} d x \geq \frac {1}{k ^ {2}}.\tag{6.67}
$$

Indeed, set 

$$
C _ {k} := \left\{x \in B _ {k}: \psi_ {k} (x) = \infty \right\}.\tag{6.68}
$$

If $| C _ { k } | = 0$ , we can simply take $w _ { k } : = \psi _ { k }$ , while if $\left| C _ { k } \right| > 0$ , then since (6.66) continues to hold on $C _ { k }$ , without loss of generality we can replace $B _ { k }$ with $C _ { k }$ . For each $x \in C _ { k }$ we define 

6 Integrands $f = f \left( x , z \right)$ 

$$
w _ {k} (x) := \min \left\{n \in \mathbb {N}: h (x, n) \leq - k n ^ {p}, n \geq \frac {1}{k ^ {\frac {2}{p}} | C _ {k} | ^ {\frac {1}{p}}} \right\}.
$$

Note that in view of (6.65) and (6.68), $w _ { k }$ is measurable and well-defined, and that (6.67) holds. 

Find Borel sets $E _ { k } \subset B _ { k }$ such that 

$$
\int_ {E _ {k}} (w _ {k}) ^ {p} d x = \frac {1}{k ^ {2}}
$$

and define 

$$
w \left(x\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} w _ {k} \left(x\right) & \text { if } x \in E _ {k}, k \in \mathbb {N}, \\ 1 & \text { otherwise }. \end{array} \right.
$$

Then $w \in L ^ { p } \left( E \right)$ , since 

$$
\int_ {E} (w) ^ {p} d x = \sum_ {k = 1} ^ {\infty} \int_ {E _ {k}} (w _ {k}) ^ {p} d x + \left| E \setminus \bigcup_ {k = 1} ^ {\infty} E _ {k} \right| \leq \sum_ {k = 1} ^ {\infty} \frac {1}{k ^ {2}} + | E | <   \infty ,
$$

while (6.67) and the fact that $h \leq 0$ yields 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \int_ {E} J (w) (x) d x = \int_ {E} h (x, w (x)) d x \leq \sum_ {k = 1} ^ {\infty} \int_ {E _ {k}} h (x, w _ {k} (x)) \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \leq - \sum_ {k = 1} ^ {\infty} \int_ {E _ {k}} k (w _ {k} (x)) ^ {p} = - \sum_ {k = 1} ^ {\infty} \frac {1}{k} = - \infty , \end{array}
$$

which contradicts Step 4. Note that we have used the fact that $w \left( E \right) \subset \mathbb { N }$ , so that $h \left( x , w \left( x \right) \right) : = J \left( w \right) \left( x \right)$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ . Hence the claim holds and there exists $k \in \mathbb N$ such that $\psi _ { k } \in L ^ { p } \left( E \right)$ 

By the definition of $\psi _ { k }$ we have that 

$$
h (x, n) > - k n ^ {p}\tag{6.69}
$$

for all $x \in E$ and all integers $n > \psi _ { k } \left( x \right)$ . Since $1 \leq \psi _ { k } \left( x \right) < \infty$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in E$ , we may find a measurable function $\psi : E \to \mathbb { N }$ that is everywhere less than or equal to $\psi _ { k }$ and such that 

$$
h \left(x, \psi (x)\right) = \min \left\{h (x, n): n \leq \psi_ {k} (x) \right\} \text {for} \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \text {a.e.} x \in E.
$$

Set $\gamma \left( x \right) : = - h \left( x , \psi \left( x \right) \right)$ . Since $0 \le \psi \le \psi _ { k } \in L ^ { p } \left( E \right)$ , by Step 4 we deduce that $\gamma \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ (where again we have used the fact that $h \left( x , \psi \left( x \right) \right) =$ $J ( \psi ) ( x ) )$ , which, together with (6.69), yields (6.52). 

By applying the previous theorem to $f$ and $- f$ we obtain necessary and suficient conditions for a superposition operator $v \mapsto f \left( \cdot , v \left( \cdot \right) \right)$ to map $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ into $L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ . Note that, in contrast to classical results in the liter ature (see Lemma 17.6 in [Kr76]), no continuity assumptions are made on $f$ in the z variable. 

Corollary 6.46 (Integral operators). Let $E \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be a Lebesgue measurable set with finite measure, let $1 \leq p < \infty$ , and let $f : E \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m }  [ - \infty , \infty ]$ be $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable. Then the superposition operator $v \mapsto f \left( \cdot , v \left( \cdot \right) \right)$ maps $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ into $L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ if and only if there exist a nonnegative function $\gamma \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ and a constant $C > 0$ such that 

$\left| f \left( x , z \right) \right| \le C \left| z \right| ^ { p } + \gamma \left( x \right)$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ and for all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ 

## 6.3.2 Well-Posedness, $p = \infty$

The proof for the case $p = \infty$ follows from the results in the previous subsection. 

Theorem 6.47. Let $E \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be a Lebesgue measurable set with finite measure, and let $f : E \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m }  [ - \infty , \infty ]$ be $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable. Then 

$$
\int_ {E} \left(f (x, v (x))\right) ^ {-} d x <   \infty
$$

for every $v \in L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ if and only if for every $M \ > \ 0$ there exists a nonnegative function $\gamma _ { M } \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ such that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq - \gamma_ {M} (x)\tag{6.70}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ with $| z | \leq M$ 

Proof. Fix $M > 0$ and define the functions 

$$
\tau_ {M} \left(z\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{c c} z & \text {if} | z | \leq M, \\ \frac {z}{| z |} M & \text {if} | z | > M, \end{array} \right.\tag{6.71}
$$

and 

$$
f _ {M} (x, z) := f (x, \tau_ {M} (z)).\tag{6.72}
$$

We claim that the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {1} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f _ {M} (x, v (x)) d x\tag{6.73}
$$

is well-defined and does not take the value $- \infty$ . Indeed, this follows from the fact that if $v \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , then $\tau _ { M } \circ v \in L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ and 

$$
\int_ {E} f _ {M} (x, v (x)) d x = \int_ {E} f (x, (\tau_ {M} \circ v) (x)) d x.
$$

By Theorem 6.45 there exist a function $a _ { M } \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ and a constant $C _ { M } > 0$ such that 

$$
f _ {M} (x, z) \geq - C _ {M} | z | - a _ {M} (x) \text {for} \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \text {a.e.} x \in E \text {and for all} z \in \mathbb {R} ^ {m}.
$$

In particular, 

$$
f (x, z) \geq - C _ {M} M - a _ {M} (x)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ and for all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ with $| z | \leq M$ 

As in the previous subsection, by applying the previous theorem to f and $- f$ we can characterize the class of operators $v \mapsto f \left( \cdot , v \left( \cdot \right) \right)$ that map $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ into $L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ 

Corollary 6.48 (Integral operators). Let $E \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be a Lebesgue measurable set with finite measure, and let $f : E \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \to [ - \infty , \infty ]$ be $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable. Then the superposition operator $v \mapsto f \left( \cdot , v \left( \cdot \right) \right) m a p s L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ into $L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ if and only if for every $M > 0$ there exists a nonnegative function $\gamma _ { M } \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ such that 

$$
| f (x, z) | \leq \gamma_ {M} (x)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ with $| z | \leq M$ 

## 6.4 Sequential Lower Semicontinuity

In this section we study necessary and suficient conditions for the sequential lower semicontinuity of functionals of the form 

$$
v \in L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f (x, v (x)) d x,\tag{6.74}
$$

where $1 \leq p \leq \infty$ and 

$$
f: E \times \mathbb {R} ^ {m} \to [ - \infty , \infty ]
$$

is $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable. 

We are interested in the following types of convergence: 

• strong convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ for $1 \leq p \leq \infty ;$ 

• weak convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ for $1 \leq p < \infty ;$ 

• weak star convergence in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ ; 

• weak star convergence in the sense of measures in $L ^ { 1 } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ 

From now on we will assume that the integrand f satisfies the appropriate growth conditions from below that are necessary and suficient to guarantee that $( f \circ v ) ^ { - } \in L ^ { 1 } ( E )$ for all $v \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , so that the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is well-defined (see Theorems 6.45 and 6.47). 

## 6.4.1 Strong Convergence in $L ^ { p } , \mathbf { 1 } \leq p < \infty$

In this subsection we study necessary and suficient conditions for the sequential lower semicontinuity of the functional (6.74) with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { p }$ 

Theorem 6.49. Let $E \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be a Lebesgue measurable set, let $1 \leq p < \infty$ , and let $f : E \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \to ( - \infty , \infty ]$ be $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times B$ measurable. Assume that there exist a nonnegative function $\gamma \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ and a constant $C > 0$ such that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq - C | z | ^ {p} - \gamma (x) \text {   for   } \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \text {   a.e.   } x \in E \text {   and   for   all   } z \in \mathbb {R} ^ {m}.\tag{6.75}
$$

Then the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ if and only if (up to equivalent integrands) $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in E$ 

Proof. Without loss of generality we may assume that there exists $v _ { 0 } ~ \in$ $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
\int_ {E} f (x, v _ {0} (x)) d x <   \infty .\tag{6.76}
$$

The proof of the suficiency part is very similar to that of Theorem 5.9, and therefore we omit it. 

We divide the proof of the necessity part into four steps. 

Step 1: We claim that for every $B \in B \left( E \right)$ the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {B} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Indeed, let $\{ v _ { n } \} \subset L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ be a sequence strongly converging to some $v \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Define 

$$
w _ {n} \left(x\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l} v _ {n} \left(x\right) \text {if} x \in B, \\ v _ {0} \left(x\right) \text {if} x \in E \setminus B, \end{array} \right. w \left(x\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l} v \left(x\right) \text {if} x \in B, \\ v _ {0} \left(x\right) \text {if} x \in E \setminus B. \end{array} \right.
$$

Then $w _ { n } \to w$ in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ and thus 

$$
\begin{array}{r l} & {\int_ {B} f (x, v) d x + \int_ {E \setminus B} f (x, v _ {0}) d x = \int_ {E} f (x, w) d x} \\ & {\qquad \leq \liminf _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {E} f (x, w _ {n}) d x} \\ & {\qquad = \liminf _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {B} f (x, v _ {n}) d x + \int_ {E \setminus B} f (x, v _ {0}) d x.} \end{array}
$$

Hence 

$$
\int_ {B} f \left(x, v\right) d x \leq \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \rightarrow \infty} \int_ {B} f \left(x, v _ {n}\right) d x,
$$

where we have used the fact that $f \left( \cdot , v _ { 0 } \left( \cdot \right) \right) \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ by (6.75) and (6.76). 

Step 2: Assume that E has finite measure and that $f \left( x , z \right) \ \geq \ 0$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ ${ \mathrm { a . e . ~ } } x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ . Fix any countable set Y of $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ and for $( x , z ) \in E { \times } \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ define 

$$
h _ {Y} \left(x, z\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} f \left(x, w \left(x\right)\right) & \text { if   there   is } w \in Y \text { such   that } w \left(x\right) = z, \\ \infty & \text { otherwise. } \end{array} \right.\tag{6.77}
$$

By Exercise 6.50, $h _ { Y }$ is $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable. Hence by Proposition 6.44(i) and (ii), where the roles of the functions s and h there are played here by the functions 

$$
s _ {Y} \left(x, z\right) := \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {w \to z} h _ {Y} \left(x, w\right), \quad (x, z) \in E \times \mathbb {R} ^ {m},\tag{6.78}
$$

and $h _ { Y }$ , respectively, there exists a normal integrand $g _ { Y } : E { \times } \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \to [ 0 , \infty ]$ such that 

$$
s _ {Y} (x, z) \leq g _ {Y} (x, z) \leq h _ {Y} (x, z)\tag{6.79}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ . By (6.77), (6.78), and (6.79), we have that 

$$
f (x, w (x)) \geq g _ {Y} (x, w (x))\tag{6.80}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ and all $w \in Y$ 

Step 3: For every $v \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ let $B \subset E$ be any Borel set such that 

$$
B \subset \left\{x \in E: g _ {Y} (x, v (x)) \in \mathbb {R} \right\}.
$$

We claim that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $w \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , with $\| w \| _ { L ^ { p } ( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } ) } \leq$ ε, and a Borel set $B _ { 1 } \subset E$ , with $| B \setminus B _ { 1 } | \leq \varepsilon$ , such that 

$$
g _ {Y} (x, v (x)) \geq f (x, v (x) + w (x)) - \varepsilon \text {for} \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \text {a.e.} x \in B _ {1}.\tag{6.81}
$$

Let $B _ { 0 }$ be the set of all points of B for which (6.79) holds for all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ and that are points of density one for E, p-Lebesgue points for v and for all functions $w \in Y$ , and points of approximate continuity for $g _ { Y } \left( x , w \left( x \right) \right)$ and $f \left( x , w \left( x \right) \right)$ for all $w \in Y$ , where all the functions in question have been extended by zero outside of E. Note that $| B \setminus B _ { 0 } | = 0$ 

Fix $\delta > 0$ . For every $x \in B _ { 0 }$ we have $g _ { Y } \left( x , v \left( x \right) \right) < \infty$ , and by (6.77), (6.78), and (6.79), there exists $v _ { x } \in Y$ such that 

$$
\left| v (x) - v _ {x} (x) \right| <   \delta , \quad g _ {Y} (x, v (x)) \geq f (x, v _ {x} (x)) - \delta .
$$

Since $x \in B _ { 0 }$ , we may find $r _ { x } > 0$ such that for all $0 < r < r _ { x }$ we have 

$$
\left\| v - v _ {x} \right\| _ {L ^ {p} (B (x, r) \cap E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} <   2 \delta \left| B (x, r) \cap E \right| ^ {1 / p},\tag{6.82}
$$

$$
\left| B (x, r) \cap \{y \in E: g _ {Y} (y, v (y)) \geq f (y, v _ {x} (y)) - 2 \delta \} \right|\tag{6.83}
$$

$$
\geq (1 - \delta) | B (x, r) \cap E |.
$$

Set $\mathcal { G } : = \{ B \left( x , r \right) : x \in B _ { 0 } , 0 < r < r _ { x } \}$ . By the Vitali-Besicovitch covering theorem there exist disjoint balls $B \left( x _ { 1 } , r _ { 1 } \right) , \ldots , B \left( x _ { k } , r _ { k } \right)$ such that 

$$
\left| B _ {0} \setminus \bigcup_ {i = 1} ^ {k} B \left(x _ {i}, r _ {i}\right) \right| \leq \delta .\tag{6.84}
$$

Define 

$$
w \left(x\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} v _ {x _ {i}} \left(x\right) - v \left(x\right) & \text { if } x \in B \left(x _ {i}, r _ {i}\right) \cap E,   i = 1, \ldots , k, \\ 0 & \text { otherwise. } \end{array} \right.
$$

By (6.82) we have 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \| w \| _ {L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} ^ {p} \leq \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} \| v _ {x _ {i}} - v \| _ {L ^ {p} (B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} ^ {p} \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \leq 2 ^ {p} \delta^ {p} \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} | B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E | \leq 2 ^ {p} \delta^ {p}   | E |  . \end{array}
$$

Let 

$$
B _ {1} := \left\{x \in E: g _ {Y} (x, v (x)) \geq f (x, v (x) + w (x)) - 2 \delta \right\}.
$$

Since $f \left( x , v \left( x \right) + w \left( x \right) \right) = f \left( x , v _ { x _ { i } } \left( x \right) \right)$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in B \left( x _ { i } , r _ { i } \right) \cap E$ , by (6.83) we have 

$$
\left| \left(B \left(x _ {i}, r _ {i}\right) \cap E\right) \setminus B _ {1} \right| \leq \delta \left| B \left(x _ {i}, r _ {i}\right) \cap E \right|
$$

and by (6.84), 

$$
\begin{array}{l} | B \setminus B _ {1} | = | B _ {0} \setminus B _ {1} | \leq \left| B _ {0} \setminus \bigcup_ {i = 1} ^ {k} B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \right| + \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} | (B (x _ {i}, r _ {i}) \cap E) \setminus B _ {1} | \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \q
$$

Hence (6.81) holds. 

Step 4: We claim that 

$$
g _ {Y} (x, z) \geq f (x, z)\tag{6.85}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ . In view of Proposition 6.24 it sufices to show that 

$$
\int_ {B} g _ {Y} (x, v) d x \geq \int_ {B} f (x, v) d x\tag{6.86}
$$

for any fixed Borel set $B \subset E$ and $v \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . If the left-hand side of (6.86) is infinite there is nothing to prove. Thus, since $g _ { Y } \geq 0$ , it sufices to consider the case that $g _ { Y } \left( \cdot , v \left( \cdot \right) \right) \in L ^ { 1 } \left( B \right)$ . Define 

$$
T := \left\{x \in B: g _ {Y} (x, v (x)) \in \mathbb {R} \right\}.
$$

Then $| B \setminus T | = 0$ . By Step $3 \ : \ : ( \mathrm { s e e \ : \ : ( 6 . 8 1 ) } )$ , for every $n \in \mathbb N$ there exists $w _ { n } \in$ $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , with $\begin{array} { r } { \left. w _ { n } \right. _ { L ^ { p } ( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } ) } \leq \frac { 1 } { 2 ^ { n } } } \end{array}$ , and a Borel set $B _ { n } \subset E$ , with $| T \setminus B _ { n } | \leq$ $\textstyle { \frac { 1 } { 2 ^ { n } } }$ , such that 

$$
g _ {Y} (x, v (x)) \geq f (x, v (x) + w _ {n} (x)) - \frac {1}{2 ^ {n}} \text {   for   } \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \text {   a.e.   } x \in B _ {n}.
$$

For any fixed integer $k \in \mathbb N$ set 

$$
C _ {k} := \bigcap_ {n > k} B _ {n}.
$$

Then $v + w _ { n }$ converges to v in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ and 

$$
g _ {Y} (x, v (x)) \geq f (x, v (x) + w _ {n} (x)) - \frac {1}{2 ^ {k}}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in C _ { k }$ for all $n > k$ . Hence by Step 1, 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \int_ {B} g _ {Y} (x, v) d x \geq \int_ {C _ {k}} g _ {Y} (x, v) d x \geq \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {C _ {k}} \left[ f (x, v + w _ {n}) - \frac {1}{2 ^ {k}} \right] d x \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \geq \int_ {C _ {k}} f (x, v) d x - \frac {1}{2 ^ {k}} | C _ {k} | \geq \int_ {C _ {k}} f (x, v) d x - \frac {1}{2 ^ {k}} | E |  , \end{array}
$$

where we have used the fact that $g _ { Y } \geq 0$ . Since $| B \setminus T | = 0$ we have 

$$
| B \setminus C _ {k} | = | T \setminus C _ {k} | \leq \sum_ {n > k} | T \setminus B _ {n} | \leq \sum_ {n > k} \frac {1}{2 ^ {n}} = \frac {1}{2 ^ {k}} \rightarrow 0
$$

as $k \to \infty$ , and so letting $k \to \infty$ and using the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem we conclude (6.86). 

Step 5: For each $k \in \mathbb N$ define the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto I _ {k} (v; E) := \int_ {E} f _ {k} (x, v (x)) d x,
$$

where 

$$
f _ {k} \left(x, z\right) := \Gamma_ {k} \left(f \left(x, z\right)\right), \quad \Gamma_ {k} \left(s\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l} k \text {   if   } s > k, \\ s \text {   if   } 0 \leq s \leq k. \end{array} \right.
$$

We claim that for every $B \in B \left( E \right)$ the functional $I _ { k } \left( \cdot ; B \right)$ is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Indeed, let $\{ v _ { n } \} \subset L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ be a sequence strongly converging to some $v \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ and set 

$$
Y := \left\{v _ {n}: n \in \mathbb {N} \right\} \cup \left\{v \right\}.
$$

By (6.80) and (6.85) we have that 

$$
f \left(x, v _ {n} (x)\right) = g _ {Y} \left(x, v _ {n} (x)\right)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ and all $n \in \mathbb { N }$ , and hence 

$$
f _ {k} (x, v _ {n} (x)) = g _ {Y, k} (x, v _ {n} (x))
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ and all $n \in \mathbb { N }$ and where $g _ { Y , k } : = \varGamma _ { k } \circ g _ { Y }$ . Since the function $g _ { Y , k } \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous, by Fatou’s lemma it follows that 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \underset {n \to \infty} {\liminf} \int_ {B} f _ {k} \left(x, v _ {n} \left(x\right)\right) d x = \underset {n \to \infty} {\liminf} \int_ {B} g _ {Y, k} \left(x, v _ {n} \left(x\right)\right) d x \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \geq \int_ {B} g _ {Y, k} \left(x, v \left(x\right)\right) d x = \int_ {B} f _ {k} \left(x, v \left(x\right)\right) d x, \end{array}
$$

and the claim is proved. 

Step 6: Consider $B \left( E \right)$ as a subset of $L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ . Since $L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ is separable we may find a countable set $S \left( E \right)$ of $B \left( E \right)$ that is dense in $B \left( E \right)$ 

Since $I _ { k } \left( \cdot ; B \right)$ is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , by Proposition 3.7 we may find a countable set $Y _ { 0 }$ of $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that for every $v \in L ^ { p } ( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } ) , B \in \mathcal { S } ( E )$ , and $k \in \mathbb N$ • 

$$
I _ {k} \left(v; B\right) = \liminf _ {w \in Y _ {0}, w \to v} I _ {k} \left(w; B\right).\tag{6.87}
$$

Hence for every $v \in L ^ { p } ( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } ) , B \in \mathcal { S } ( E )$ , and $k \in \mathbb N$ , by (6.87), (6.80), and (6.85), and again using Fatou’s lemma we have 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \int_ {B} f _ {k} (x, v (x)) d x = \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {w \in Y _ {0}, w \to v} \int_ {B} f _ {k} (x, w (x)) d x \\ \qquad = \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {w \in Y _ {0}, w \to v} \int_ {B} g _ {Y _ {0}, k} (x, w (x)) d x \\ \qquad \geq \int_ {B} g _ {Y _ {0}, k} (x, v (x)) d x. \end{array}
$$

Since $0 \leq f _ { k } , g _ { Y _ { 0 } , k } \leq k$ and $S \left( E \right)$ is dense in $B \left( E \right)$ , the previous inequality holds for every $B \in B \left( E \right)$ and thus by Proposition 6.24 we have that 

$$
f _ {k} (x, z) \geq g _ {Y _ {0}, k} (x, z)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ and $k \in \mathbb N$ . By letting $k \to \infty$ we conclude that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq g _ {Y _ {0}} (x, z)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ , which, together with (6.85), establishes the necessity part of the theorem in the case that E has finite measure and $f \geq 0$ 

Step 7: In the case that E has finite measure but f can take negative values, by (6.75) we have that the function 

$$
g (x, z) := f (x, z) + C | z | ^ {p} + \gamma (x)
$$

is nonnegative, $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable, and the functional 

$$
H (v; B) := \int_ {B} f (x, v) + C | v | ^ {p} + \gamma (x) d x
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Hence, by Steps 1–6, $f \left( x , \cdot \right) + C \left| \cdot \right| ^ { p } + \gamma \left( x \right)$ is lower semicontin uous, and in turn, $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous. 

Step 8: Finally, if E has infinite measure, then by Step 1 we can apply Steps $2 ^ { - 7 }$ to the set $E \cap B \left( 0 , j \right)$ for each $j \in \mathbb N$ . This completes the proof of the necessity part. 

Exercise 6.50. Prove that the function $h _ { Y }$ defined in Step 2 of the previous proof is $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable. 

As in the previous subsection, by applying the previous theorem to f and $- f$ we can characterize the class of all continuous operators $v \mapsto f \left( \cdot , v \left( \cdot \right) \right)$ that map $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ into $L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ 

Corollary 6.51 (Continuity of integral operators). Let $E \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be a Lebesgue measurable set, let $1 \leq p < \infty$ , and let $f : E \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \to [ - \infty , \infty ]$ be $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \mathcal { B }$ measurable. Assume that there exist a nonnegative function $\gamma \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ and a constant $C > 0$ such that 

$$
| f (x, z) | \leq C | z | ^ {p} + \gamma (x) \text {   for   } \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \text {   a.e.   } x \in E \text {   and   for   all   } z \in \mathbb {R} ^ {m}.
$$

Then the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is continuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ if and only if $( u p$ to equivalent integrands) $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is continuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ 

## 6.4.2 Strong Convergence in $\mathbf { \nabla } L ^ { \infty }$

When $p = \infty$ we have an analogous result. 

Theorem 6.52. Let $E \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be a Lebesgue measurable set, and let $f : E \times$ $\mathbb { R } ^ { m } \to ( - \infty , \infty ]$ be $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable. Assume that for every $M > 0$ there exists a nonnegative function $\gamma _ { M } \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ such that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq - \gamma_ {M} (x)\tag{6.88}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ with $| z | \leq M$ . Then the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {\infty} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ if and only if (up to equivalent integrands) $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in E$ 

Proof. Without loss of generality we may assume that there exists $v _ { 0 } ~ \in$ $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
\int_ {E} f (x, v _ {0} (x)) d x <   \infty .
$$

The suficiency part of the theorem follows from Fatou’s lemma. To prove the necessity part, we start by observing that as in Step 1 of the proof of the previous theorem, we may assume, without loss of generality, that for every $B \in B \left( E \right)$ the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {\infty} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {B} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Also, by Step 8 it is enough to consider the case that $E$ has finite measure. 

Fix $M > 0$ and consider the function $f _ { M }$ defined in (6.72) and the corresponding functional defined in (6.73). By (6.88) the function $f _ { M }$ satisfies (6.75) with $p = 1$ . We claim that the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {1} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f _ {M} (x, v (x)) d x\tag{6.89}
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { 1 } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Indeed, let $\{ v _ { n } \} \subset L ^ { 1 } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ be any a sequence converging strongly in $L ^ { 1 } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ to some $v \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Without loss of generality we may assume that 

$$
\operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {E} f _ {M} \left(x, v _ {n} \left(x\right)\right) d x = \lim _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {E} f _ {M} \left(x, v _ {n} \left(x\right)\right) d x
$$

and then extract a subsequence (not relabeled) of $\{ v _ { n } \}$ that converges to v pointwise $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. in $E$ . 

Fix $\varepsilon > 0$ . By Egorof’s theorem there exists a set $B _ { \varepsilon } \subset E$ such that $| B _ { \varepsilon } | < \varepsilon$ and $v _ { n }$ converges uniformly to $v$ in $E \setminus B _ { \varepsilon }$ . Define 

$$
w _ {n} := \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} v _ {n} \text {   on   } E \setminus B _ {\varepsilon}, \\ v \text {   on   } B _ {\varepsilon}. \end{array} \right.
$$

Then the sequence $\{ \tau _ { M } \circ w _ { n } \}$ converges in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ to $\tau _ { M } \circ v$ , where $\tau _ { M }$ is the function defined as in (6.71). By hypothesis it follows that 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {E} \left[ f _ {M} \left(x, v _ {n}\right) + \gamma_ {M} \right] d x \geq \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {E \setminus B _ {\varepsilon}} \left[ f _ {M} \left(x, v _ {n}\right) + \gamma_ {M} \left(x\right) \right] d x \\ = \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {E \setminus B _ {\varepsilon}} \left[ f \left(x, \tau_ {M} \circ w _ {n}\right) + \gamma_ {M} \left(x\right) \right] d x \\ \geq \int_ {E \setminus B _ {\varepsilon}} \left[ f \left(x, \tau_ {M} \circ v\right) + \gamma_ {M} \left(x\right) \right] d x \\ = \int_ {E \setminus B _ {\varepsilon}} \left[ f _ {M} \left(x, v\right) + \gamma_ {M} \left(x\right) \right] d x. \end{array}
$$

Letting $\varepsilon \to 0 ^ { + }$ we conclude that 

$$
\liminf _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {E} f _ {M} \left(x, v _ {n}\right) d x \geq \int_ {E} f _ {M} \left(x, v\right) d x
$$

and the claim is proved. Since the functional (6.89) satisfies all the hypotheses of the previous theorem, we have that $f _ { M } \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ 

Choose $M _ { k } : = k$ and let $N _ { k } \subset E$ with $| N _ { k } | = 0$ be such that $f _ { M _ { k } } \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for all $x \in E \setminus N _ { k }$ . Define 

$$
N _ {0} := \bigcup_ {k = 1} ^ {\infty} N _ {k}.
$$

Then $| N _ { 0 } | = 0$ . We claim that $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for all $x \in E \setminus N _ { 0 }$ . Indeed, fix $x \in E \setminus N _ { 0 }$ and let $\{ z _ { n } \} \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ be such that $z _ { n }  z$ and take $M _ { k } > | z _ { n } |$ for all n. Then 

$$
\liminf _ {n \to \infty} f \left(x, z _ {n}\right) = \liminf _ {n \to \infty} f _ {M _ {k}} \left(x, z _ {n}\right) \geq f _ {M _ {k}} \left(x, z\right) = f \left(x, z\right).
$$

This completes the proof. 

The analogue of Corollary 6.51 is the following result. 

Corollary 6.53 (Continuity of integral operators). Let $E \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be a Lebesgue measurable set and let $f : E \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m }  [ - \infty , \infty ]$ be $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \mathcal { B }$ measurable. Assume that for every $M > 0$ there exists a nonnegative function $\gamma _ { M } \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ such that 

$$
| f (x, z) | \leq \gamma_ {M} (x)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ with $| z | \leq M$ . Then the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {\infty} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is continuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ if and only if (up to equivalent integrands) $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is continuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ 

## 6.4.3 Weak Convergence in $L ^ { p } , \mathbf { 1 } \leq p < \infty$

We study necessary and suficient conditions for sequential lower semicontinuity with respect to weak convergence in $L ^ { p } ( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } ) , 1 \le p < \infty$ , and weak star convergence in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Since functionals that are sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to weak convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ (respectively weak star when $p = \infty )$ are also sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to strong convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , without loss of generality, in what follows we may assume that the integrand f satisfies all the necessary conditions for strong convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ obtained in the previous subsections. 

Theorem 6.54. Let $E \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be a Lebesgue measurable set, let $1 \leq p < \infty$ and let $f : E \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m }  ( - \infty , \infty ]$ be $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable. Assume that $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous in R<sup>m</sup> for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ } a . e . \mathrm { ~ } x \in E$ and that there exist a nonnegative function $\gamma \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ and a constant $C > 0$ such that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq - C | z | ^ {p} - \gamma (x) \text {for} \mathcal {L} ^ {N} a. e. x \in E \text {and for all} z \in \mathbb {R} ^ {m}.
$$

Then the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to weak convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ if and only if 

(i) $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is convex in R<sup>m</sup> for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ ; 

(ii) there exist two functions $a \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ and $b \in L ^ { p ^ { \prime } } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq a (x) + b (x) \cdot z
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ 

Proof $( S u f f i c i e n c y )$ . Without loss of generality we may assume that there exists $v _ { 0 } \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
\int_ {E} f (x, v _ {0} (x)) d x <   \infty .
$$

The proof is very similar to the suficiency proof of Theorem 5.14 and we only indicate the main changes. As in Step 2 we can assume, without loss of generality, that $f \left( x , z \right) \geq 0$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ . Using the blowup method as in Step 1 of the suficiency proof of Theorem 5.14 we need to show only that 

$$
\frac {d \mu}{d \mathcal {L} ^ {N}} (x _ {0}) = \lim _ {\varepsilon \rightarrow 0 ^ {+}} \frac {\mu (Q (x _ {0} , \varepsilon) \cap E)}{\varepsilon^ {N}} \geq f (x _ {0}, v (x _ {0})) \quad \text { for } \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \text { a.e. } x _ {0} \in E.
$$

By Theorem 6.39 there exist two sequences of bounded measurable functions 

$$
a _ {i}: E \to \mathbb {R}, \quad b _ {i}: E \to \mathbb {R} ^ {m},
$$

such that 

$$
f (x, z) = \sup _ {i \in \mathbb {N}} \left\{a _ {i} (x) + b _ {i} (x) \cdot z \right\}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ 

Fix a point $x _ { 0 } ~ \in ~ E$ of density one for E that satisfies (5.15) and is a Lebesgue point of all the $L _ { \mathrm { l o c } } ^ { 1 }$ functions $a _ { i } \left( \cdot \right) \chi _ { E } \left( \cdot \right)$ and $\left( b _ { i } ( \cdot ) \cdot v \left( \cdot \right) \right) \chi _ { E } \left( \cdot \right)$ Then as in (5.18) we can conclude that 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \frac {d \mu}{d \mathcal {L} ^ {N}} (x _ {0}) = \lim _ {k \to \infty} \frac {\mu (Q (x _ {0} , \varepsilon_ {k}) \cap E)}{\varepsilon_ {k} ^ {N}} \\ \qquad = \lim _ {k \to \infty} \lim _ {n \to \infty} \frac {1}{\varepsilon_ {k} ^ {N}} \int_ {Q (x _ {0}, \varepsilon_ {k}) \cap E} f (x, v _ {n} (x))   d x \\ \qquad \geq \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {k \to \infty} \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \frac {1}{\varepsilon_ {k} ^ {N}} \int_ {Q (x _ {0}, \varepsilon_ {k}) \cap E} (a _ {i} (x) + b _ {i} (x) \cdot v _ {n} (x))   d x \\ \qquad = \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {k \to \infty} \frac {1}{\varepsilon_ {k} ^ {N}} \int_ {Q (x _ {0}, \varepsilon_ {k}) \cap E} (a _ {i} (x) + b _ {i} (x) \cdot v (x))   d x \\ \qquad = a _ {i} (x _ {0}) + b _ {i} (x _ {0}) \cdot v (x _ {0}), \end{array}
$$

where we have used the fact that $v _ { n } \to v$ in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . By taking the supremum over all i we conclude that 

$$
\frac {d \mu}{d \mathcal {L} ^ {N}} (x _ {0}) \geq f (x _ {0}, v (x _ {0}))
$$

as desired. 

Proof (Necessity). Without loss of generality, we may assume that there exists $v _ { 0 } \in L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
\int_ {E} f (x, v _ {0} (x)) d x <   \infty ,\tag{6.90}
$$

and, replacing $f \left( x , z \right)$ with $f \left( x , z - v _ { 0 } \left( x \right) \right)$ , that $v _ { 0 } = 0$ . As in the proof of Step 1 of Theorem 6.49, we can show that for every $B \in B \left( E \right)$ the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {p} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {B} f (x, v (x)) d x\tag{6.91}
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to weak convergence in $L ^ { p } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ 

Step 1: We claim that $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is convex in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { a . e . } x \in E$ . We consider first the case that $| E | < \infty$ . Fix $\theta \in [ 0 , 1 ] \cap \mathbb { Q }$ and let v, $w \in L ^ { \infty } ( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ Let $\left\{ h _ { n } \right\}$ be a sequence of functions in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \{ 0 , 1 \} \right)$ such that (see Example 2.86) 

$$
h _ {n} \stackrel {*} {\rightharpoonup} \theta \quad \text { in } L ^ {\infty} (E).
$$

For $x \in E$ define 

$$
u _ {n} (x) := \left(1 - h _ {n} (x)\right) v (x) + h _ {n} (x) w (x).
$$

Then $u _ { n } \stackrel { * } {  } u$ in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , where 

$$
u (x) := (1 - \theta) v (x) + \theta w (x),
$$

and so by the sequential lower semicontinuity of the energy (6.91), for every $B \in B \left( E \right)$ we have 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \int_ {B} f (x, (1 - \theta) v (x) + \theta w (x)) d x \leq \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {B} f (x, u _ {n} (x)) d x \\ = \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {B} (1 - h _ {n} (x)) f (x, v (x)) + h _ {n} (x) f (x, w (x)) d x \\ = (1 - \theta) \int_ {B} f (x, v (x)) d x + \theta \int_ {B} f (x, w (x)) d x. \end{array}
$$

Since this is true for all $B \in B \left( E \right)$ and $v , \ w \in L ^ { \infty } ( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ , it follows from Proposition 6.24 that there exists a set $N _ { \theta } \subset E$ , with $| N _ { \theta } | = 0$ , such that 

$$
f (x, (1 - \theta) z + \theta w) \leq (1 - \theta) f (x, z) + \theta f (x, w)\tag{6.92}
$$

for all $x \in E \setminus N _ { \theta }$ and all $z , w \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ . Let 

$$
N _ {0} := \bigcup_ {\theta \in [ 0, 1 ] \cap \mathbb {Q}} N _ {\theta}.
$$

Then $| N _ { 0 } | = 0$ and (6.92) holds for all $\theta \in [ 0 , 1 ] \cap \mathbb { Q } , x \in E \setminus N _ { 0 }$ , and all $z ,$ $w \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ . Now fix $\theta \in [ 0 , 1 ]$ and let $\theta _ { n } \in [ 0 , 1 ] \cap \mathbb { Q }$ be such that $\theta _ { n } \to \theta$ . By (6.92), 

$$
f \left(x, \left(1 - \theta_ {n}\right) z + \theta_ {n} w\right) \leq \left(1 - \theta_ {n}\right) f (x, z) + \theta_ {n} f (x, w)
$$

for all $n \in \mathbb { N } , x \in E \setminus N _ { 0 }$ , and all $z , w \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ . By letting $n \to \infty$ and using the fact that $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { \bar { N } } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ we prove the claim in the case $\vert E \vert < \infty . \mathrm { I f } \left. E \right. = \infty$ and in view of the sequential lower semicontinuity of the energy (6.91) it sufices to apply the first part of this step to $| E \cap B \left( 0 , j \right) |$ for each $j \in \mathbb N$ 

Step 2: Replacing $f \left( x , z \right)$ with $\begin{array} { r } { \frac { 1 } { p C } \left( f \left( x , z \right) - \gamma \left( x \right) \right) } \end{array}$ , we may assume, without loss of generality, that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq - \frac {1}{p} | z | ^ {p} \text {   for   } \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \text {   a.e.   } x \in E \text {   and   for   all   } z \in \mathbb {R} ^ {m}.
$$

Thus for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { a . e . } x \in E$ we may apply Proposition 5.16 to define two functions $a : E \to [ 0 , \infty ) , b : E \to \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ such that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq a (x) + b (x) \cdot z \geq - \frac {1}{p} | z | ^ {p} \mathrm{for} \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \mathrm{a.e.} x \in E \mathrm{andall} z \in \mathbb {R} ^ {m}.\tag{6.93}
$$

By Aumann’s selection theorem we may assume that a and b are measurable. Moreover, if $p = 1$ , then $| b \left( x \right) | \leq 1$ , while for $p > 1$ , 

$$
\left| b (x) \right| ^ {p ^ {\prime}} \leq C (p) a (x)\tag{6.94}
$$

for some constant $C \left( p \right) > 0$ . It remains to show that $a \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ , which by (6.94) will entail $b \in L ^ { p ^ { \prime } } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ ). Taking $z = 0$ in (6.93), it follows that 

$$
f (x, 0) \geq a (x) \geq 0,
$$

which, by (6.90), implies that $a \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ 

Remark 6.55. Note that the proof of the suficiency still holds under $L ^ { \infty }$ weak star convergence for nonnegative $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \mathcal { B }$ measurable integrands $f : E \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m } $ $[ 0 , \infty ]$ such that $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous and convex in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in E$ 

## 6.4.4 Weak Star Convergence in $\mathbf { \nabla } L ^ { \infty }$

The case $p = \infty$ follows from the results in the previous subsections. 

Theorem 6.56. Let $E ~ \subset ~ \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be a Lebesgue measurable set, and let $f :$ $E \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \to ( - \infty , \infty ]$ be $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \boldsymbol { B }$ measurable. Assume that $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is lower semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \ \in \ E$ and that for every $M > 0$ there exists a nonnegative function $a _ { M } \in L ^ { 1 } \left( E \right)$ such that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq - a _ {M} (x)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ with $| z | \leq M$ . Then the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {\infty} (E; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {E} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to weak star convergence in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ if and only if $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is convex in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in E$ 

Proof. To prove suficiency, let $v _ { n } \stackrel { * } {  } v$ in $L ^ { \infty } \left( E ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Then 

$$
\sup _ {n} \left\| v _ {n} \right\| _ {L ^ {\infty} (\varOmega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} \leq M
$$

for some $M > 0$ , and so 

$$
f \left(x, v _ {n} (x)\right) \geq - a _ {M} (x)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in E$ and all $n \in \mathbb { N }$ . Define 

$$
f _ {M} (x, z) := \max \left\{f (x, z), - a _ {M} (x) \right\}.
$$

Note that 

$$
f \left(x, v _ {n} (x)\right) = f _ {M} \left(x, v _ {n} (x)\right) \quad \text { and } \quad f \left(x, v (x)\right) = f _ {M} \left(x, v (x)\right)
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in E$ , all $n \in \mathbb { N }$ , and 

$$
f _ {M} (x, z) + a _ {M} (x)
$$

is a nonnegative $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \times \mathcal { B }$ measurable function, convex and lower semicontinuous in the z variable. By Remark 6.55 we have 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {E} f (x, v _ {n}) d x = \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {E} [ f _ {M} (x, v _ {n}) + a _ {M} (x) ] d x - \int_ {E} a _ {M} (x) d x \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \geq \int_ {E} [ f _ {M} (x, v) + a _ {M} (x) ] d x - \int_ {E} a _ {M} (x) d x \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad = \int_ {E} f (x, v) d x. \end{array}
$$

The proof of the necessity condition is entirely identical to that of Theorem 6.54. 

## 6.4.5 Weak Star Convergence in the Sense of Measures

In this subsection we consider only the case in which the domain of integration is an open subset $\varOmega \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ . As we remarked in Section 5.2.3, due to lack of reflexivity of the space $L ^ { 1 } ( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ ), if $\{ v _ { n } \} \subset L ^ { 1 } ( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ is such that 

$$
\sup _ {n} \left\| v _ {n} \right\| _ {L ^ {1}} <   \infty ,
$$

then one can conclude only that $\{ v _ { n } \}$ admits a subsequence (not relabeled) such that $v _ { n } { \mathcal { L } } ^ { N } | ~ \varOmega ~ { \stackrel { * } { \to } } ~ \lambda$ in $\mathcal { M } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , i.e., if for all $u \in C _ { 0 } \left( \varOmega \right)$ 

$$
\int_ {\Omega} u v _ {n} d x \rightarrow \int_ {\Omega} u d \lambda .
$$

This subsection is devoted to the study of sequential lower semicontinuity under this natural notion of convergence. In particular, we will address necessary and suficient conditions under which the lower semicontinuity property 

$$
\operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {\Omega} f \left(x, v _ {n}\right) d x \geq \int_ {\Omega} f \left(x, \frac {d \lambda}{d \mathcal {L} ^ {N}}\right) d x
$$

holds whenever $v _ { n } { \mathcal { L } } ^ { N } \mid \varOmega \ \stackrel { * } {  } \ \lambda$ in $\mathcal { M } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ and λ admits the Radon– Nikodym decomposition 

6 Integrands $f = f \left( x , z \right)$ 

$$
\lambda = \frac {d \lambda}{d \mathcal {L} ^ {N}} \mathcal {L} ^ {N} \left\lfloor \Omega + \lambda_ {s}, \right.
$$

with $\lambda _ { s }$ and $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ mutually singular. 

Since functionals that are sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to this type of convergence are also sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to weak convergence in $L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , without loss of generality we may assume in what follows that the integrand f satisfies all the necessary condi tions for weak convergence in $L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ (see the previous subsection). 

In what follows, to each function ψ : $\varOmega \to \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ we associate the multifunction $\Gamma _ { \psi } : \varOmega \to \mathcal { P } \left( \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right) \backslash \{ \emptyset \}$ defined by 

$$
\Gamma_ {\psi} (x) := \{\psi (x) \}, \quad x \in \Omega .
$$

Theorem 6.57. Let $\varOmega \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be an open set and let $f : \varOmega \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \to [ - \infty , \infty ]$ be Borel measurable. Assume that $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is convex and lower semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \ \in \ \mathcal { \Omega }$ and that there exist a function $a \in L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega \right)$ and a constant $C > 0$ such that 

$$
f (x, z) \geq a (x) + C | z |\tag{6.95}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in \varOmega$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ . Then the functional 

$$
v \in L ^ {1} (\Omega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}) \mapsto \int_ {\Omega} f (x, v (x)) d x
$$

is sequentially lower semicontinuous with respect to weak star convergence in the sense of measures if and only if 

$$
f (x, z) = \tilde {f} (x, z)\tag{6.96}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \ a . e . \ x \in \varOmega$ and al $, z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ , where 

$$
\tilde {f} (x, z) := \sup _ {\xi \in \Gamma (x)} [ \xi \cdot z - f ^ {*} (x, \xi) ], \quad (x, z) \in (\Omega , \mathbb {R} ^ {m}),\tag{6.97}
$$

and Γ is the essential supremum of the family of multifunctions $\mathcal { F } : =$ $\{ \boldsymbol { T } _ { \psi } : \psi \in \mathcal { X } \}$ (with respect to the Lebesgue measure), where 

$$
\mathcal {X} := \left\{\psi \in C _ {0} (\Omega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}): f ^ {*} (\cdot , \psi (\cdot)) \in L ^ {1} (\Omega) \right\},
$$

and $f ^ { * } \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is the polar function of $f \left( x , \cdot \right)$ 

More generally, if (6.96) holds, then for any sequence $\{ v _ { n } \} \subset L ^ { 1 } ( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ such that $v _ { n } { \mathcal { L } } ^ { N } | ~ \varOmega ~ { \stackrel { * } { \to } } ~ \lambda$ in $\mathcal { M } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ we have 

$$
\operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {\Omega} f \left(x, v _ {n}\right) d x \geq \int_ {\Omega} f \left(x, \frac {d \lambda}{d \mathcal {L} ^ {N}}\right) d x + \int_ {\Omega} f _ {s} \left(x, \frac {d \lambda}{d \left\| \lambda_ {s} \right\|}\right) d \left\| \lambda_ {s} \right\|,\tag{6.98}
$$

where 

$$
f _ {s} (x, z) := \sup \left\{\psi (x) \cdot z: \psi \in \mathcal {X} \right\}\tag{6.99}
$$

for all $x \in \varOmega$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ 

Remark 6.58. Often in the literature 

$$
\liminf _ {n \to \infty} \int_ {\Omega} f \left(x, v _ {n}\right) d x \geq \int_ {\Omega} f \left(x, \frac {d \lambda}{d \mathcal {L} ^ {N}}\right) d x + \int_ {\Omega} f ^ {\infty} \left(x, \frac {d \lambda}{d \left\| \lambda_ {s} \right\|}\right) d \left\| \lambda_ {s} \right\|
$$

is written in place of (6.98). A word of caution is needed here: although 

$$
\int_ {\Omega} f (x, v (x)) d x = \int_ {\Omega} \tilde {f} (x, v (x)) d x
$$

for every $v \in L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , it may happen that 

$$
f ^ {\infty} (x, \cdot) \neq f _ {s} (x, \cdot)\tag{6.100}
$$

on a set of Lebesgue measure zero E for which $\left\| \lambda _ { s } \right\| \left( E \right) > 0$ for some measure λ. 

See the next exercise. 

Exercise 6.59. An example of (6.100) is given by 

$$
f \left(x, z\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} | z | & \text {if} | z | \sqrt {| x |} \leq 1, \\ 2 | z | - \frac {1}{\sqrt {| x |}} & \text {if} | z | \sqrt {| x |} > 1, \end{array} \right.
$$

for $x \in ( - 1 , 1 )$ and $z \in \mathbb { R }$ . Prove that $f _ { s } \neq f ^ { \infty }$ 

To prove Theorem 6.57 we need some preliminary results. 

Proposition 6.60. Let $\varOmega \subset \mathbb { R } ^ { N }$ be an open set, let $g : \varOmega \times \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \to ( - \infty , \infty ]$ be Borel measurable, and let $\nu : \mathfrak { M } \left( \varOmega \right) \to \left[ 0 , \infty \right)$ be a positive finite Radon measure. Assume that there exist two functions $a \ \in \ L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega , \nu \right)$ and $b \in$ $L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega , \nu ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
g (x, z) \geq a (x) + b (x) \cdot z\tag{6.101}
$$

for ν a.e. $x \in \varOmega$ and $a l l \ z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ . Suppose further that $g \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is convex and lower semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\nu \ a . e . \ x \in \varOmega$ , and let 

$$
\mathcal {X} _ {g, \nu} := \left\{\psi \in C _ {0} (\Omega): g (\cdot , \psi (\cdot)) \in L ^ {1} (\Omega , \nu) \right\}.\tag{6.102}
$$

$I f \mathcal { X } _ { g , \nu } \neq \emptyset$ , then 

$$
\inf _ {\psi \in \mathcal {X} _ {g, \nu}} \int_ {\Omega} g (x, \psi (x)) d \nu = \int_ {\Omega} \hat {g} (x) d \nu ,\tag{6.103}
$$

where 

$$
\hat {g} (x) := \inf _ {\xi \in \Gamma_ {\nu} (x)} g (x, \xi)
$$

and $\varGamma _ { \nu }$ is the essential supremum of the family of multifunctions $\mathcal { F } : =$ $\{ T _ { \psi } : \psi \in \mathcal { X } _ { g , \nu } \}$ with respect to ν. In addition, 

6 Integrands $f = f \left( x , z \right)$ 

$$
\hat {g} (x) = \inf _ {n \in \mathbb {N}} g (x, \psi_ {n} (x))\tag{6.104}
$$

for $\nu \ a . e . \ x \in \varOmega$ whenever 

$$
\Gamma_ {\nu} (x) = \overline {{\{\psi_ {n} (x) \}}}
$$

for $\nu \ a . e . \ x \in \varOmega$ 

Proof. Note that the convexity of $g \left( x , \cdot \right)$ together with (6.101) implies that the family $\chi _ { g , \nu }$ is convex. Hence by Remark 6.14, $\varGamma _ { \nu } \left( x \right)$ is convex and there exists a sequence $\{ \psi _ { n } \} \subset \mathcal { X } _ { g , \nu }$ such that 

$$
\Gamma_ {\nu} (x) = \overline {{\{\psi_ {n} (x) \}}}\tag{6.105}
$$

for $\nu \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in \varOmega$ . Define 

$$
N _ {0} := \Omega \setminus \bigcup_ {n = 1} ^ {\infty} \left\{x \in \Omega : g (x, \psi_ {n} (x)) \in \mathbb {R} \right\}.
$$

By (6.102) the set $N _ { 0 }$ has ν measure zero, and by Proposition 4.41 and (6.105), 

$$
\hat {g} (x) = \inf _ {n \in \mathbb {N}} g (x, \psi_ {n} (x))\tag{6.106}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in \varOmega$ . It follows that the function $\hat { g }$ is measurable. Moreover, for any $\psi \in \mathcal { X } _ { g , \nu }$ we have that $\psi \left( x \right) \in { \varGamma _ { \nu } } \left( x \right)$ for $\nu \ \mathrm { a . e . } \ x \in \varOmega$ , and so 

$$
g (x, \psi (x)) \geq \hat {g} (x)
$$

for $\nu \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in \varOmega$ . By (6.102) it follows that $( \hat { g } ) ^ { + } \in L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega , \nu \right)$ ; thus 

$$
\inf _ {\psi \in \mathcal {X} _ {g, \nu}} \int_ {\Omega} g (x, \psi (x)) d \nu \geq \int_ {\Omega} \hat {g} (x) d \nu ,
$$

where the right-hand side is well-defined. To prove the reverse inequality let $t \in \mathbb { R }$ be such that 

$$
t > \int_ {\Omega} \hat {g} (x) d \nu .
$$

Then 

$$
\int_ {\Omega} (\hat {g}) ^ {-} (x) d \nu > \int_ {\Omega} (\hat {g}) ^ {+} (x) d \nu - t,
$$

and so by applying Proposition 1.92 to the function $\left( { \hat { g } } \right) ^ { - }$ we may find a simple function $s \in L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega , \nu \right)$ such that $0 \leq s \leq ( \hat { g } ) ^ { - }$ in $\varOmega$ with 

$$
\int_ {\Omega} s (x) d \nu > \int_ {\Omega} (\hat {g}) ^ {+} (x) d \nu - t.
$$

Then the function $\alpha : = ( \hat { g } ) ^ { + } - s$ belongs to $L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega , \nu \right) , \alpha \left( x \right) \geq \hat { g } \left( x \right)$ for $\nu \ \mathrm { a . e . }$ $x \in \varOmega$ , and 

$$
t > \int_ {\Omega} \alpha (x) d \nu .\tag{6.107}
$$

By the Vitali–Carath´eodory theorem we may assume that α is lower semicontinuous. 

Fix $w _ { 0 } \in \mathcal X _ { g , \nu }$ . By (6.102), for any fixed $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a compact set $K \subset \varOmega \setminus N _ { 0 }$ such that 

$$
\int_ {\Omega \backslash K} | g (x, w _ {0} (x)) | + | \alpha (x) | d \nu <   \varepsilon ,\tag{6.108}
$$

and a number $\delta > 0$ such that 

$$
\int_ {E} | g (x, w _ {0} (x)) | + | \alpha (x) | d \nu <   \varepsilon\tag{6.109}
$$

for all $E \subset { \mathcal { Q } }$ with $\nu \left( E \right) < \delta$ . By Lusin’s theorem for each $n \in \mathbb N$ there exists a compact set $K ^ { ( n ) } \ { \stackrel { \cdot } { \subset } } \ K$ with $\nu \left( K \setminus K ^ { ( n ) } \right) \ < \ \frac { \delta } { 2 ^ { n } }$ such that $g \left( \cdot , \psi _ { n } \left( \cdot \right) \right)$ is continuous on $K ^ { ( n ) }$ . Let 

$$
K _ {\varepsilon} := \bigcap_ {n = 1} ^ {\infty} K ^ {(n)}.
$$

Then $\nu \left( K \setminus K _ { \varepsilon } \right) < \delta$ and $g \left( \cdot , \psi _ { n } \left( \cdot \right) \right)$ is continuous on $K _ { \varepsilon }$ for all $n \in \mathbb N$ . Let $\eta > 0$ be small enough that $\eta \nu \left( K \right) < \varepsilon ,$ , and for every $n \in \mathbb N$ set 

$$
E _ {n} := \left\{x \in K _ {\varepsilon}: g (x, \psi_ {n} (x)) <   \alpha (x) + \eta \right\}.\tag{6.110}
$$

Since each function $g \left( \cdot , \psi _ { n } \left( \cdot \right) \right) - \alpha \left( \cdot \right)$ is upper semicontinuous in $K _ { \varepsilon }$ , the set $E _ { n }$ is relatively open in $K _ { \varepsilon }$ , and by (6.106) and the fact that $\alpha \geq \hat { g }$ , we have 

$$
K _ {\varepsilon} = \bigcup_ {n = 1} ^ {\infty} E _ {n}.
$$

By compactness there exists $\ell \in \mathbb { N }$ such that 

$$
K _ {\varepsilon} = \bigcup_ {n = 1} ^ {\ell} E _ {n}.
$$

Let $A _ { \varepsilon } \subset \joinrel \subset \varOmega$ be an open set such that $A _ { \varepsilon } \supset K _ { \varepsilon }$ and 

$$
\int_ {A _ {\varepsilon} \backslash K _ {\varepsilon}} (g (x, \psi_ {n} (x))) ^ {+} d \nu <   \frac {\varepsilon}{\ell}\tag{6.111}
$$

for all $n = 1 , \ldots , \ell .$ . Since the sets $E _ { n }$ are relatively open in $K _ { \varepsilon }$ we may find open sets $A _ { n } \subset A _ { \varepsilon }$ such that $A _ { n } \cap K _ { \varepsilon } = E _ { n }$ . Construct a partition of unity $\varphi _ { 0 } , \ldots , \varphi _ { \ell } \in C \left( { \overline { { \Omega } } } \right)$ with 

$$
\sum_ {n = 0} ^ {\ell} \varphi_ {n} \equiv 1 \mathrm{on} \overline {{A _ {\varepsilon}}}
$$

such that supp $\varphi _ { n } \subset A _ { n }$ for all $n = 1 , \ldots , \ell .$ , and supp $\varphi _ { 0 } \subset \mathcal { Q } \setminus K _ { \varepsilon }$ . Since $\varphi _ { 0 } = 1$ on $\partial A _ { \varepsilon }$ we may define $\varphi _ { 0 }$ continuously to be identically equal to one in $\mathcal { \Omega } \setminus \overline { { A _ { \varepsilon } } }$ . Hence now 

$$
\sum_ {n = 0} ^ {\ell} \varphi_ {n} \equiv 1 \mathrm{in} \Omega
$$

and 

$$
\psi := \varphi_ {0} w _ {0} + \sum_ {n = 1} ^ {\ell} \varphi_ {n} \psi_ {n} \in \mathcal {X} _ {g, \nu}
$$

by the convexity of $g \left( x , \cdot \right)$ , (6.101), and (6.102). Moreover, again by the con vexity of $g \left( x , \cdot \right)$ we have 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \int_ {\Omega} g (x, \psi (x)) d \nu \leq \int_ {\Omega} \varphi_ {0} (x) g (x, w _ {0} (x)) d \nu + \sum_ {n = 1} ^ {\ell} \int_ {\Omega} \varphi_ {n} (x) g (x, \psi_ {n} (x)) d \nu \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \leq \int_ {\Omega \setminus K _ {\varepsilon}} | g (x, w _ {0} (x)) | d \nu + \sum_ {n = 1} ^ {\ell} \int_ {K _ {\varepsilon}} \varphi_ {n} (x) g (x, \psi_ {n} (x)) d \nu \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad + \sum_ {n = 1} ^ {\ell} \int_ {A _ {\varepsilon} \setminus K _ {\varepsilon}} (g (x, \psi_ {n} (x))) ^ {+} d \nu \\ \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \leq 2 \varepsilon + \int_ {K _ {\varepsilon}} (\alpha (x) + \eta) d \nu + \varepsilon \leq t + 6 \varepsilon , \end{array}
$$

where we have used (6.107), (6.108), (6.109), (6.110), and (6.111). Hence 

$$
\inf _ {w \in \mathcal {X} _ {g, \nu}} \int_ {\Omega} g (x, w (x)) d \nu \leq t + 6 \varepsilon .
$$

By letting first $\varepsilon \to 0 ^ { + }$ and then $t \searrowint _ { \Omega } \hat { g } \left( x \right)$ dν we conclude that 

$$
\inf _ {\psi \in \mathcal {X} _ {g, \nu}} \int_ {\Omega} g (x, \psi (x)) d \nu \leq \int_ {\Omega} \hat {g} (x) d \nu .
$$

This completes the proof. 

Remark 6.61. The analogue of (6.103) holds for supremum in place of infimum provided there exist two functions $a \in L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega , \nu \right)$ and $b \in L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega , \nu ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ such that 

$$
g (x, z) \leq a (x) + b (x) \cdot z
$$

for $\nu \ \mathrm { a . e . } \ x \ \in \ \varOmega$ and all $z \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ , and that $g \left( x , \cdot \right)$ is concave and upper semicontinuous in $\mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ for $\nu \ \mathrm { a . e . } \ x \in \varOmega$ . In this case, 

$$
\sup _ {\psi \in \mathcal {X} _ {g, \nu}} \int_ {\Omega} g (x, \psi (x)) d \nu = \int_ {\Omega} \check {g} (x) d \nu ,
$$

where 

$$
\check {g} (x) := \sup _ {\xi \in \Gamma_ {\nu} (x)} g (x, \xi)
$$

and $\varGamma _ { \nu }$ is still the essential supremum of the family of multifunctions $\mathcal { F } : =$ $\{ T _ { \psi } : \psi \in \mathcal { X } _ { g , \nu } \}$ with respect to ν. In addition, 

$$
\check {g} (x) = \sup _ {n \in \mathbb {N}} g (x, \psi_ {n} (x))\tag{6.112}
$$

for $\nu \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in \varOmega$ whenever 

$$
\Gamma_ {\nu} (x) = \overline {{\{\psi_ {n} (x) \}}}
$$

for $\nu \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in \varOmega$ 

The next exercise illustrates the fact that in the previous theorem $\chi _ { g , \ l }$ ν cannot be taken to be the entire space $C _ { 0 } \left( \varOmega \right)$ 

Exercise 6.62. Let $\varOmega = \mathbb { R } , m = 1$ 

(i) Construct a compact set $K \subset \mathbb { R }$ with empty interior and such that $| K | >$ 0. 

(ii) Define 

$$
g \left(x, z\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} z & \text {if} x \in K, \\ I _ {\{0 \}} \left(z\right) & \text {otherwise}, \end{array} \right.
$$

where $I _ { \{ 0 \} }$ is the indicator function of {0}, namely 

$$
I _ {\{0 \}} (z) = \left\{ \begin{array}{l l} 0 & \text { if } z = 0, \\ \infty & \text { otherwise }. \end{array} \right.
$$

Prove that 

$$
\inf _ {\psi \in C _ {0} (\mathbb {R})} \int_ {\Omega} g (x, \psi (x)) d \nu = 0.
$$

(iii) Prove that the essential supremum of the family of multifunctions $\mathcal { F } : =$ $\{ T _ { \psi } : \psi \in C _ { 0 } \left( \mathbb { R } \right) \}$ is the multifunction 

$$
\Gamma_ {\nu} (x) \equiv \mathbb {R}
$$

for $x \in \mathbb { R }$ 

(iv) Prove that (6.103) fails. 

Proof (Necessity of Theorem $6 . 5 7 )$ . Without loss of generality we may assume that there exists $v _ { 0 } \in L ^ { 1 } ( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ such that 

$$
\int_ {\Omega} f (x, v _ {0} (x)) d x <   \infty .\tag{6.113}
$$

Since $L ^ { 1 } ( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ may be identified with a subspace of $\mathcal { M } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ that is the dual of the separable space $C _ { 0 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , by (6.95) we are in a position to apply Proposition 3.16 to conclude that the functional 

$$
I (v) := \int_ {\Omega} f (x, v) d x, \quad v \in L ^ {1} (\Omega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}),
$$

is lower semicontinuous with respect to weak star convergence. 

Consider now the duality pair $\left( L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right) , C _ { 0 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right) \right)$  <sub>under the duality</sub> 

$$
\langle u, \phi \rangle_ {L ^ {1} (\varOmega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}), C _ {0} (\varOmega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} := \int_ {\varOmega} u \cdot \phi d x
$$

for $u \in L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ and $C _ { 0 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ . Then the functional I is convex and lower semicontinuous with respect to the topology $\sigma \left( L ^ { 1 } , C _ { 0 } \right)$ . It follows from Proposition 4.92, taking as V the topological vector space 

$$
\left(L ^ {1} \left(\Omega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m}\right), \sigma \left(L ^ {1}, C _ {0}\right)\right),
$$

that $I = I ^ { * * }$ 

Since by Theorem A.72 the topological dual of $\left( L ^ { 1 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right) , \sigma \left( L ^ { 1 } , C _ { 0 } \right) \right)$ is $C _ { 0 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , if $v \in L ^ { 1 } ( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ , then 

$$
I (v) = I ^ {* *} (v) = \sup _ {\psi \in C _ {0} (\Omega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} \left[ \int_ {\Omega} \psi \cdot v d x - I ^ {*} (\psi) \right].\tag{6.114}
$$

Step 1: We claim that for $\psi \in C _ { 0 } \left( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } \right)$ , 

$$
I ^ {*} (\psi) = \int_ {\Omega} f ^ {*} (x, \psi (x)) d x.\tag{6.115}
$$

Note that by (6.95) and (6.113) the function 

$$
\gamma (x) := - f (x, v _ {0} (x))\tag{6.116}
$$

belongs to $L ^ { 1 } ( \varOmega )$ and since 

$$
f ^ {*} (x, \xi) \geq \xi \cdot v _ {0} (x) + \gamma (x)\tag{6.117}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N } \mathrm { ~ a . e . ~ } x \in \varOmega$ and all $\xi \in \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ , by Proposition 6.43 the right-hand side of (6.115) is well-defined. 

By Definition 4.86 we have 

$$
I ^ {*} (\psi) = \sup _ {v \in L ^ {1} (\Omega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} \int_ {\Omega} (\psi \cdot v - f (x, v)) d x.\tag{6.118}
$$

Since 

$$
f ^ {*} (x, \xi) = \sup _ {w \in \mathbb {R} ^ {m}} [ \xi \cdot w - f (x, w) ],
$$

then 

$$
I ^ {*} (\psi) \leq \int_ {\Omega} f ^ {*} (x, \psi (x)) d x.
$$

To prove the reverse inequality, let $t \in \mathbb { R }$ be such that 

$$
\int_ {\Omega} f ^ {*} (x, \psi (x)) d x > t
$$

and fix $\varepsilon > 0$ . Let 

$$
E _ {\infty} := \{x \in \Omega : f ^ {*} (x, \psi (x)) = \infty \}
$$

and consider first the case $| E _ { \infty } | > 0$ . Let $K \subset E _ { \infty }$ be any compact set with positive measure, and using Aumann’s selection theorem and the definition of $f ^ { * }$ select a measurable function $w : K  \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ such that 

$$
\psi (x) \cdot w (x) - f (x, w (x)) \geq \frac {2}{| K |} \left(t + \int_ {\Omega} | \psi \cdot v _ {0} + \gamma | d y\right)\tag{6.119}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in K$ . By Lusin’s theorem there exists a compact set $K _ { \varepsilon } \subset K$ with $\begin{array} { r } { | K \setminus K _ { \varepsilon } | < \frac { | K | } { 2 } } \end{array}$ such that w is continuous on $K _ { \varepsilon }$ . Define 

$$
v _ {\varepsilon} \left(x\right) := \left\{ \begin{array}{l} w \left(x\right) \text { if } x \in K _ {\varepsilon}, \\ v _ {0} \left(x\right) \text { if } x \in \varOmega \setminus K _ {\varepsilon}. \end{array} \right.\tag{6.120}
$$

Then $v _ { \varepsilon } \in L ^ { 1 } ( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ , and by (6.116) and (6.119), 

$$
\begin{array}{c} \int_ {\Omega} (\psi \cdot v _ {\varepsilon} - f (x, v _ {\varepsilon})) d x \geq \frac {2 | K _ {\varepsilon} |}{| K |} \left(t + \int_ {\Omega} | \psi \cdot v _ {0} + \gamma | d y\right) \\ - \int_ {\Omega \setminus K _ {\varepsilon}} | \psi \cdot v _ {0} + \gamma | d x \geq t, \end{array}
$$

and so 

$$
I ^ {*} (\psi) = \sup _ {\varpi \in L ^ {1} (\Omega ; \mathbb {R} ^ {m})} \left[ \int_ {\Omega} \psi \cdot \varpi d x - \int_ {\Omega} f (x, \varpi) d x \right] \geq t.
$$

Given the arbitrariness of t we conclude that 

$$
I ^ {*} (\psi) \geq \int_ {\Omega} f ^ {*} (x, \psi (x)) d x.\tag{6.121}
$$

If $| E _ { \infty } | = 0$ , then find a compact set $K \subset \varOmega$ such that 

$$
\int_ {K} f ^ {*} (x, \psi (x)) d x > t, \quad \int_ {\Omega \backslash K} | \psi \cdot v _ {0} + \gamma | d x <   \varepsilon ,\tag{6.122}
$$

and a number $\delta = \delta \left( \varepsilon \right) > 0$ such that 

6 Integrands $f = f \left( x , z \right)$ 

$$
\int_ {E} | \psi \cdot v _ {0} + \gamma | d x <   \varepsilon\tag{6.123}
$$

for all $E \subset { \mathcal { Q } }$ with $| E | < \delta$ . The function $\delta$ may be assumed to be increasing with $\varepsilon > 0$ 

As before, let $w : K  \mathbb { R } ^ { m }$ be a measurable function such that 

$$
f ^ {*} (x, \psi (x)) \leq \psi (x) \cdot w (x) - f (x, w (x)) + \frac {\varepsilon}{| K |}\tag{6.124}
$$

for $\mathcal { L } ^ { N }$ a.e. $x \in K$ , and by Lusin’s theorem find a compact set $K _ { \varepsilon } \subset K$ with $| K \setminus K _ { \varepsilon } | < \delta$ such that w is continuous on $K _ { \varepsilon }$ . Choose $K _ { \varepsilon }$ in such a way that if $\varepsilon < \varepsilon ^ { \prime }$ , then $K _ { \varepsilon } \supset K _ { \varepsilon ^ { \prime } }$ . Define $v _ { \varepsilon }$ as in (6.120). Then $v _ { \varepsilon } \in L ^ { 1 } ( \varOmega ; \mathbb { R } ^ { m } )$ , and by (6.116) and (6.124), 

$$
\begin{array}{l} \int_ {\Omega} (\psi \cdot v _ {\varepsilon} - f (x, v _ {\varepsilon})) d x \\ \geq \int_ {K _ {\varepsilon}} f ^ {*} (x, \psi) d x - \varepsilon - \int_ {\Omega \setminus K _ {\varepsilon}} | \psi \cdot v _ {0} + \gamma | d x \\ = \int_ {K _ {\varepsilon}} (f ^ {*} (x, \psi)) ^ {+} d x - \int_ {K _ {\varepsilon}} (f ^ {*} (x, \psi)) ^ {-} d x \\ \quad - \varepsilon - \int_ {\Omega \setminus K _ {\varepsilon}} | \psi \cdot v _ {0} + \gamma | d x \\ \geq \int_ {K _ {\varepsilon}} (f ^ {*} (x, \psi)) ^ {+} d x - \int_ {K} (f ^ {*} (x, \psi)) ^ {-} d x \\ \quad - \varepsilon - \int_ {\Omega \setminus K} | \psi \cdot v _ {0} + \gamma | d x \\ \geq \int_ {K _ {\varepsilon}} (f ^ {*} (x, \psi)) ^ {+} d x - \int_ {K} (f ^ {*} (x, \psi)) ^ {-} d x - 3 \varepsilon , \end{array}
$$

where we have used (6.122) and (6.123). 

By (6.118) we deduce that 

$$
I ^ {*} (\psi) \geq \int_ {K _ {\varepsilon}} (f ^ {*} (x, \psi)) ^ {+} d x - \int_ {K} (f ^ {*} (x, \psi)) ^ {-} d x - 3 \varepsilon ,
$$
